## 3. Verified source record

The complete JSON entry below is copied from the current local source. Preserve its id, author_id, author_name, day, hour, knowledge_key, timestamp, and exact text. Candidate prose is editorial material, not part of the loaded row.

```json
{
  "id": "journal_raw_b3_02_plumber_the_freeze_line",
  "text": "The feed line to the cistern froze last night at the elbow where it comes through the foundation wall. I have been telling the Architect since Day 90 that the insulation on that elbow is insufficient. She said there was no insulation left. There is no insulation left. So I wrapped it in three layers of salvaged blanket and a sheet of the rubber pond liner the Botanist was using for the mushroom trays. She was not happy about the pond liner. I was not happy about the freeze. The line thawed by midday with a hot-water pour. If it had cracked we would have lost the cistern feed and been on bucket duty from the lower sump. That is eight flights of stairs per bucket. I do not want to think about it. I am going to find insulation. I do not know where. I am going to find it.",
  "timestamp": "Day 121, 14h",
  "author_name": "The Plumber",
```

## 4. Fixed canon and open space

The cistern feed froze at the elbow through the foundation wall, was wrapped with salvaged blanket and pond liner, and thawed after a hot-water pour. A crack would have meant bucket duty from the lower sump, eight flights per bucket. The Plumber says he will find insulation but does not know where. Do not add a source or claim the line is permanently safe. Candidate language may add an image, rhythm, or private impression as an editorial draft, but no proposed addition becomes a further remembered event or a confirmed fact until the existing content owner selects and reviews it against the source.

## 5. Human center

The source voice is The Plumber. The Plumber speaks in practical repetition, naming the elbow, the salvaged layers, and the stairs that would follow a break. Keep the persistence concrete; finding insulation is a promise to search, not a result. The prose may notice what the author can count, hear, repair, fear, or leave uncertain, while keeping the account’s limits visible.
